paragraphs.source_en: In contrast to Keenan (2003: 195) who states that the Tassili is almost entirely devoid of portable artefacts, and in contradiction with Holl (2004: 3) who claims that with a handful of exceptions localities with drawings are devoid of other kinds of archaeological residue, my fieldwork has shown the abundance of lithic artefacts both in painted sites and outside them. With the exception of grinding stones that are very rare indeed, the whole study area presents a huge amount of lithic tools ranging from large rough ones to tiny microliths. Lhote (1958: 57) states that painted shelters at Jabbaren contain hundreds of grinding stones, however, I have not found any of these archaeological artefacts at this site. Grinding stones as well as other easily recognisable archaeological material were frequently transported to private collections both in Algeria and in Europe.

paragraphs.source_en: The lithic tools that were found inside the sites were present near the painted walls as well as in other areas such as corridors or squares. The typology of the lithic industry found on the surface is the same as that unearthed during excavation in the study area (Aumassip 1980-1; Barich 1987; Cremaschi, & Di Lernia 1998) and it includes the Epipalaeolithic, Mesolithic and Pastoral industries (Fig. 3-10). There are no known sites which only have artefacts from one period which indicates that the painted sites and their surroundings were frequented during a very long time span. Besides lithic tools, potsherds of circa 2-3 cm were found in some sites, most often with impressed motifs of dots and short lines, however, no entire vessel was found.
